title: Categorical processing of Chinese lexical tone: ECoG auditory oddball in 6 epilepsy patients (Si, Zhou & Hong 2017)
description: Electrocorticography (ECoG) recordings from six patients with medically intractable epilepsy who passively listened to a two-deviant auditory oddball sequence of synthesized Mandarin syllables. The tone continuum allowed comparison of a cross-category deviant (rising vs level tone) with a within-category deviant at equal physical distance from the standard, probing categorical processing of Chinese lexical tone. Data are provided in iEEG-BIDS format without signal processing.
methods_description: ECoG was recorded at 1200 Hz with 96 ECoG inputs and 6 trigger inputs per file while patients watched a silent movie. A synthesized rising-level-falling tone continuum of Mandarin /i/ was used, with token 5 (level tone T1) as the frequent standard and tokens 2 (rising T2) and 8 (level T1) as infrequent deviants. There were 500 trials (250 for S6), with a 1100 ms onset-to-onset interval and 5% jitter. Electrode placement was determined by clinical need only. Note: the source release does not document the trigger event codes; the mapping of codes 1/2/3 to standard / cross-category deviant / within-category deviant is inferred from stimulus file names and code frequencies.
